record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: Can one prove an analog of the Toda stopping-time universality theorem for the full deflation time T_{ε,n,A,E} of some eigenvalue algorithm A, where deflation requires control of more of the eigenvector structure and not only the top eigen-gap?

evidence.quote: The most challenging problem for eigenvalue computation with random data is to prove the analog of Theorem 1 for the deflation time Tε,n,A,E ... for some algorithm A.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $E$ be an ensemble of $n\times n$ real symmetric or complex Hermitian random matrices (for example a Wigner ensemble with i.i.d. entries of mean zero and finite variance). Let $A$ be a deterministic eigenvalue algorithm acting on Hermitian matrices that produces, starting from $M_0=M$ drawn from $E$, a sequence of isospectral iterates $M_0,M_1,M_2,\dots$ converging to a diagonal matrix (e.g. the Toda flow sampled at integer times, the QR algorithm, or the QR algorithm with shifts).

Halting (top‑gap) time. For $\varepsilon>0$, define the top‑gap halting time
$$\tau_{\varepsilon,n,A,E}(M)=\min\Bigl\{k\ge 0\ :\ \bigl|(M_k)_{n,n-1}\bigr|<\varepsilon\Bigr\},$$
which measures the first time the off‑diagonal entry coupling the last eigenvalue to the rest of the spectrum has dropped below $\varepsilon$.

Deflation time. Define the full deflation time
$$T_{\varepsilon,n,A,E}(M)=\min\Bigl\{k\ge 0\ :\ \max_{1\le j\le n-1}\bigl|(M_k)_{j+1,j}\bigr|<\varepsilon\Bigr\},$$
that is, the first iteration at which every sub‑diagonal entry of $M_k$ is smaller than $\varepsilon$, so that all eigenvalues have been numerically separated.

Known result (top‑gap universality). For $A$ equal to the Toda algorithm, there exist scaling constants $a_n=a_n(\varepsilon,A,E)$, $b_n=b_n(\varepsilon,A,E)$ and a distribution function $F_A$, independent of the choice of $E$ within a wide universality class, such that
$$\frac{\tau_{\varepsilon,n,A,E}-a_n}{b_n}\ \Longrightarrow\ F_A\qquad(n\to\infty).$$

Problem. Prove (or disprove) the analogous universality statement for the full deflation time: namely, exhibit an eigenvalue algorithm $A$ (e.g. Toda, QR, or QR with shifts), scaling constants $\widetilde a_n,\widetilde b_n$, and a distribution function $G_A$ such that
$$\frac{T_{\varepsilon,n,A,E}-\widetilde a_n}{\widetilde b_n}\ \Longrightarrow\ G_A\qquad(n\to\infty)$$
holds with $G_A$ independent of $E$ across an appropriate universality class (e.g. Wigner ensembles with sufficient moments). Unlike the top‑gap case, a proof must control not only the topmost spectral gap but also the joint behavior of all sub‑diagonal entries, equivalently the localization/delocalization and rigidity properties of the entire eigenvector basis throughout the iteration.
artifact.status_search_result: Rigorous universality has been established (Deift–Trogdon, 2016, and subsequent works including the recent monograph on the Toda lattice and universality) for the halting time associated with computing the largest eigenvalue (top eigen-gap) via the Toda algorithm, and analogous results for sample covariance matrices. However, the analog for the full deflation time—where all sub-diagonal entries must drop below ε and finer control of the full eigenvector basis is required—does not appear to have been proved for any eigenvalue algorithm; it remains a stated central open problem in this line of work.

status_evidence.title: Universality for the Toda algorithm to compute the largest eigenvalue of a random matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Universality is proved for the fluctuations of the halting time for the Toda algorithm to compute the largest eigenvalue of real symmetric and complex Hermitian matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Universality is established only for the top-gap halting time, not the full deflation time.

status_evidence.title: The Toda Lattice and Universality for the Computation of the Eigenvalues of a Random Matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes universality for the associated Toda eigenvalue algorithm for random Hermitian matrices.
status_evidence.claim: The current rigorous treatment covers the Toda halting time; the full-deflation analog is not asserted.

status_evidence.title: Universality in numerical computation with random data
status_evidence.snippet: Empirical universality observed for the normalized deflation time across Wigner ensembles, but rigorous proof remains for the top-gap case.
status_evidence.claim: Universality of the full deflation time is observed numerically but not proven.
